status: confirmed as filed — severity critical upheld, cited line exact, no chain break
title: docker-compose JWT_SECRET default does not match the value checked by the security warning — admin tokens are forgeable with a repo-published key and no warning is ever printed
category: authentication / cryptographic failure (key management, broken fail-safe)
evidence: docker-compose.yml:15 verbatim `      - JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:-CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET}` (uppercase placeholder) vs. backend/internal/config/config.go:63 `JWTSecret:          getenv("JWT_SECRET", "change-me-jwt-secret"),` and backend/cmd/server/main.go:188 `if cfg.JWTSecret == "change-me-jwt-secret" {` (case-sensitive equality, no normalization). config.go:30-35 `func getenv(k, def string) string { if v := os.Getenv(k); v != "" { return v } ... }` — compose injects a non-empty uppercase value, so the Go default and the only warning trigger are both bypassed. Verification: docker-compose.yml read end-to-end (38 lines); config.go read end-to-end (76 lines); main.go read end-to-end (216 lines, warnInsecureDefaults called unconditionally at main.go:83); backend/internal/admin/middleware.go read end-to-end (33 lines, line 23 verbatim `claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, token)`); backend/internal/auth/jwt.go read end-to-end (44 lines); backend/internal/admin/configstatus.go read end-to-end (71 lines, no secret check); backend/internal/admin/routes.go read end-to-end (196 lines; only routes.go:42 `api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)` is unauthenticated). grep `(?i)change-me` over the repo finds the uppercase string ONLY in docker-compose.yml:15-16 (+ README variants at another placeholder), so no code anywhere recognizes it; grep `jti|WithIssuer|WithAudience|revoc|blacklist` over backend/ → zero matches. Reachability: quickstart.en.md:82-86 `docker compose up -d`, .env.template:3-4 (all vars optional; compose auto-reads ./.env), Dockerfile:22-30 sets no JWT_SECRET env and `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/server"]`.
impact: A default `docker compose up -d` (no .env / no exported JWT_SECRET) signs every admin JWT with the literal `CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET`, published in this repository, while the admin API is published on 0.0.0.0:8080 (docker-compose.yml:10 `- "${PORT:-8080}:8080"`). An unauthenticated attacker HMACs `{"uid":1,"uname":"admin","exp":<future>}` with that string and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; admin/middleware.go:23 accepts it — the middleware verifies only the signature/exp and never loads the AdminUser row, sets `operator`/`userID` straight from attacker-chosen claims (middleware.go:29-30), and there is no role/permission layer, so one forged token reaches all ~70 admin routes. auth/jwt.go:31-33 pins SigningMethodHMAC, so no alg confusion is needed or possible — the public key is the whole vulnerability. Concretely: mint gateway keys (`sk-` plaintext returned once at apikeys.go:54), exfiltrate every upstream provider key by pointing base_url at an attacker host (providers.go:110-111 keeps the victim's APIKeyEnc unless a new one is sent) and then POST /providers/:id/test, which decrypts (providers.go:163) and transmits it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (providers.go:180) or `x-api-key` (providers.go:177) — after which all live gateway traffic also flows to the attacker (runtime/manager.go:214-215); read/export all call logs and payloads; create+download full DB backups; take permanent ownership via PUT /auth/password (auth.go:157-184) and strip other admins' second factor via POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa (routes.go:134). The forged token also defeats MFA outright: auth.go:86-108 gates only the login handler and the Claims struct (jwt.go:11-15) has no amr/mfa claim. It is also silent and sticky: warnInsecureDefaults never fires for this value and configstatus.go has no security field, so operators get no log line and no UI banner — while .env.template:19 and frontend/src/i18n/locales/en-US/pages/help.ts:47 affirmatively promise 'startup prints a [security] WARNING' for default keys, and quickstart.en.md:240 lists that warning as the *only* detection signal. Because the key is per-deployment-static and there is no jti/revocation anywhere, changing ADMIN_PASSWORD or enabling MFA does not evict the attacker, and no legitimate token can be distinguished from a forged one in the audit trail (the log records `operator: "admin"` from the attacker's own claim).
why_new_beyond_known_architecture: The standing note 'JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY defaults are warn-only' presumes the warning actually fires for the deployed default. It does not on the container path: the shipped compose fallback is a different, uppercase string, so (a) the only bounding control is absent, (b) the documented `docker compose up -d` flow is the zero-config flow the project advertises, and (c) the standard remediation ('set a strong ADMIN_PASSWORD') leaves token forgery permanently available. This is a defect in the fail-safe itself, not a restatement of a disclosed default.
mitigations_checked: auth/jwt.go:31-33 pins `*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC` → 'none'/RS256 confusion impossible (does not help: the secret is public). Parse passes no validation options, so iss/iat are unenforced even though Issue sets `Issuer: "llm-router-guard"` (jwt.go:23) — no cross-deployment constraint. exp IS enforced (24h, jwt.go:21) but the attacker simply re-mints. No jti/blacklist/revoke store (grep → 0 matches). middleware.go does no user-existence/lock check, so `IsLocked()` (auth.go:38-41) is login-only and cannot contain a forged token. warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) exists but its literal never matches; it is non-blocking by design anyway, so even a correct match would only log. No CORS/network separation compensates: same-origin single process serves /api/admin/v1 and /v1 on one port (routes.go:17-41) and the finding does not rely on a browser. No startup validation of JWT_SECRET length/entropy anywhere in config.Load(). Bootstrap note: crypto.NewCipher (crypto.go:21-32, plain sha256 KDF) accepts the placeholder MASTER_KEY, so the container does boot in this state — the vulnerable configuration is reachable, not crash-gated.
report_corrections: Impact wording tightened: provider API keys are not returned in plaintext by GET /providers or GET /config/export (model.go:107-108 both `json:"-"`; bundle.go:15 'keys kept as DB ciphertext'); exfil requires PUT /providers/:id (base_url swap) + POST /providers/:id/test (providers.go:163+180) or offline decryption of a downloaded backup using the equally-undetected compose MASTER_KEY.
'gateway keys' = newly minted plaintext via POST /apikeys (apikeys.go:39-54); existing keys are SHA-256-only (model.go:37 `KeyHash ... json:"-"`) and cannot be recovered.

The finding's precedent 'compose already uses ${VAR:?} for REDIS_PASSWORD at line 37' is inside the commented-out block at docker-compose.yml:34-38, so it is not live in the shipped file; the real precedent is README.md:284-287 (`JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:?set-jwt-secret}`).

Additional undetected placeholder the original missed: README.md:160-161 / README.zh-CN.md:162-163 use `${JWT_SECRET:-replace-with-random-secret}`, which main.go:188 also cannot match; README.md:45 documents only the lowercase Go default, so the repo contradicts itself about which key a container uses.
recommendation: (1) docker-compose.yml:15-16 → `JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:?JWT_SECRET must be set}` / `MASTER_KEY=${MASTER_KEY:?MASTER_KEY must be set}` so a published placeholder can never sign anything; (2) replace warnInsecureDefaults' equality test with a case-insensitive deny-set of every placeholder in the repo (both cases + `replace-with-*`), and refuse to start in gin.ReleaseMode when JWT_SECRET is empty or in that set (config.Load currently has no such gate); (3) log a SHA-256 prefix of the effective JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY at boot and surface a 'using_default_secret' boolean in /api/admin/v1/status so the SPA can render a persistent banner instead of the currently-false assurance in help.ts:47; (4) defense-in-depth: add a per-admin token epoch/jti so a leaked signing key can be neutralized without redeploy, and validate `iss`.

verifies: derived during verification of authn-1 (same defect class, different variable)
status: new sub-finding established while reading docker-compose.yml:16 against main.go:191 and crypto.NewCipher
title: Identical case-mismatch silently disables the MASTER_KEY default warning on the container path: provider keys are AES-GCM-encrypted under a repo-published master key with no operator signal
category: key management / broken fail-safe (defense-in-depth gap with real impact)
evidence: docker-compose.yml:16 verbatim `      - MASTER_KEY=${MASTER_KEY:-CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY}` vs. backend/internal/config/config.go:64 `MasterKey:          getenv("MASTER_KEY", "llm-router-guard-master-key"),` and backend/cmd/server/main.go:191 `if cfg.MasterKey == "llm-router-guard-master-key" {`. crypto.go:21-23 `func NewCipher(masterKey string) (*Cipher, error) { sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(masterKey))` — any non-empty string is accepted, so the container boots and derives a fixed, reproducible AES-256 key from the published placeholder. Every provider secret is produced by this cipher: providers.go:64 `enc, err := s.enc.Encrypt(req.APIKey)` stored in `APIKeyEnc` (model.go:107), decrypted on the hot path at runtime/manager.go:214 and in providers.go:163.
impact: For the documented `docker compose up -d` path the encryption master key for all upstream provider API keys is `CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY`, and warnInsecureDefaults line 191 can never match it, so no `[security] WARNING` is printed and the operator is told (en-US/pages/help.ts:47, .env.template:19) that a warning would appear. Anyone who obtains the ciphertext at rest — the SQLite file under the compose bind mount `${DATA_DIR_PATH:-./data}:/app/data` (docker-compose.yml:26) via any host/backup/`GET /api/admin/v1/backups/:id/download` exposure, or `bundle.go` exports — decrypts every provider key offline with a key taken from the public repo, defeating the 'keys are AES-GCM encrypted at rest (REQ-005 ④)' control entirely. Reachable independently of verify-authn-1-1 (backup-file theft / directory leak / DB exfil do not require a valid token to be *meaningless* once the master key is public), which is why it is graded medium rather than folded away: it removes the only remaining confidentiality property of the stored-credential design. It also makes master-key rotation invisible: because the warning never fires, an operator has no signal that rotation (which main.go:192 warns requires re-entering providers) is mandatory.
mitigations_checked: AES-GCM itself is correctly implemented (crypto.go:34-41 random 12-byte nonce per Encrypt via io.ReadFull(rand.Reader), base64 output; Decrypt rejects short ciphertexts, crypto.go:48-50), so the failure is purely key secrecy; `APIKeyEnc`/`APIKey` are excluded from all JSON responses (model.go:107-108) so the key is not disclosed by the API, and MaskKey (providers.go:70) shows only a masked form; providers.go:130 clears `p.APIKeyEnc = ""` before the update response. No integrity/authenticated-keystore or KMS option exists (config.go:64 is the only key source), and no code path validates MASTER_KEY strength or entropy. Grep confirms `CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY` appears nowhere in Go code, so no detection exists.
recommendation: Same fix as verify-authn-1-1 for symmetry: `MASTER_KEY=${MASTER_KEY:?MASTER_KEY must be set}` in docker-compose.yml:16, plus a case-insensitive placeholder deny-set (including `llm-router-guard-master-key`, `replace-with-master-key`, `CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY`) checked in config.Load, with a hard refusal to boot in release mode on a placeholder master key. Longer term: derive with a KDF that proves intent (or accept a base64 32-byte key and reject anything shorter than 32 bytes of entropy), log the SHA-256 prefix of the active master key at boot, and add a key-version column on providers so rotation is verifiable rather than 're-enter every provider'.
